title: Environment-specific IAM playbook + SIEM field mapping
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a practical playbook covering: 1) a compact env-specific IAM role matrix for RBAC v2, 2) short policy template variants for hosted / dedicated / private, 3) the audit-log -> SIEM export field mapping we want to standardize, and 4) a lightweight evidence automation flow for access reviews and investigations. Intention: give engineering, SRE, and compliance owners a single-page reference plus runbook steps to instrument evidence exports and alerts.

Executive summary (TL;DR):
- RBAC v2 pulls away from static org-wide roles; we define role families (read, write, admin, deploy, audit) and then specialize them by environment: hosted, dedicated, private.
- Hosted: multi-tenant API plane + managed infra. Access is principle-of-least-privilege (PLP) with fine-grained API keys.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with customer isolation; additional network and capacity management permissions.
- Private: full customer-managed control plane; ops team needs remote troubleshooting privileges but only with ephemeral sessioning and HSM/KMS controls.
- SIEM mapping: unify field names for user_id, session_id, request_path, model_version, env_tag, decision (allow/deny), reason_code; this makes dashboarding and automated evidence extraction deterministic.

1) RBAC v2: condensed environment-role matrix (human-readable)
Format: RoleFamily | Hosted | Dedicated | Private | Example principals
- Viewer | read:instances, read:models, read:billing-metrics | read:instances, read:models, read:dedicated-usage | read:instances, read:models, read:private-configs | analysts, auditors
- Developer | read:models, write:prompts, create:routes (dev) | read:models, write:routes, start:jobs (bounded) | read:models, write:routes (no infra tweak) | eng-devs, feature-teams
- Operator | manage:routes, restart:pods, view:kvcache-stats | manage:capacity-pools, ops:scaling, swap-images | manage:onprem-nodes (ephemeral), network-ops | infra/oncall
- Admin | all:* (scoped to tenant for hosted), tenant:config:* | all:* within dedicated account | all:* within private environment but gated by JIT/Bastion | security leads, infra-platform
Notes on scoping and naming: always include env_tag labels in role bindings (env:hosted, env:dedicated:customer-123, env:private:customer-xyz). RBAC v2 policy IDs should follow pattern: rbacv2.<team>.<role>.<env>.<version>. Example: rbacv2.infra.operator.dedicated.v2

2) Policy template snippets (short, explanatory)
- Hosted (principle): limited tenant-level control; no host-level ssh, no KMS key creation
Snippet (pseudo-YAML):
  - role: hosted-operator
    allowed_actions: ["deploy:model-version","rollback:route","view:metrics"]
    deny_actions: ["create:kms-key","attach-network-peering"]
    resource_scope: "tenant:${TENANT_ID}/*"
    conditions: ["time:business-hours?false","mfa:required"]

- Dedicated (principle): ops can manage capacity and deployments; must not modify customer-managed KMS unless explicitly delegated
Snippet: 
  - role: dedicated-capacity-manager
    allowed_actions: ["scale:pool","set:burst-capacity","assign:gpus"]
    allowed_resources: ["capacity-pool:${POOL_ID}","model:${MODEL_ID}"]
    network_constraints: ["only-from:ops-vpc-cidr"]

- Private (principle): full control but gated by ephemeral session + audit evidence must be attached to privileged sessions
Snippet:
  - role: private-admin
    allowed_actions: ["manage:nodes","configure:network","kms:use"]
    preconditions: ["session:ephemeral","evidence:mrn_required"]
    enforcement: ["attach-audit-trace","require-hsm-backed-kms"]

3) Audit log schema canonical fields (for ingestion into SIEM)
We standardize on these keys (name -> type -> short description). These will be the canonical names used in all exporters.
- timestamp -> RFC3339 -> event time
- event_id -> UUID -> unique event identifier
- actor_id -> string -> internal user id (pref: azure/okta subject id or internal uid)
- actor_name -> string -> display name if available
- principal_type -> enum(user, service, api_key, system)
- env_tag -> string -> hosted|dedicated:customer-123|private:customer-xyz
- tenant_id -> string -> customer/tenant id when applicable
- ip_address -> string -> source IP
- session_id -> string -> ephemeral session id or api key id
- action -> string -> canonical action (e.g. create:route, deploy:model, kms:encrypt)
- resource -> string -> resource path or arn-like identifier
- model_version -> string -> model id + version if applicable
- decision -> enum(allow, deny, error) -> enforcement outcome
- reason_code -> string -> short code for denial or error (e.g. DENY_ROLE, DENY_NETWORK)
- auth_method -> string -> oauth|api_key|saml|mfa|hsm
- request_latency_ms -> integer -> total handling time in ms
- request_payload_hash -> string -> sha256 of request body (for quick diff, optional)
- evidence_refs -> array-string -> list of evidence artifact ids (transcript, session-recording)
- related_ids -> array-string -> correlated event ids
Implementation notes: SIEM expects flat JSON lines. evidence_refs and related_ids should be exported as comma-separated strings in legacy pipelines.

4) SIEM export mapping (example for Splunk/Elastic)
Goal: consistent dashboards and deterministic extraction for audits.
- actor.identity -> actor_id
- user.name -> actor_name
- host.environment -> env_tag
- event.action -> action
- event.outcome -> decision
- network.client.ip -> ip_address
- rule.reason -> reason_code
- kpi.latency_ms -> request_latency_ms
- audit.evidence_refs -> evidence_refs (CSV string)
- mapping should be implemented in the exporter layer (ingest lambda / log-forwarder), not in each service, to reduce divergence.

5) Evidence automation flow (lightweight runbook)
Triggering events: failed privileged attempt (decision=deny and action in [manage:nodes, kms:use, configure:network]) OR elevated-group-binding created OR admin-role-granted.
Automated steps:
  1) Export 24h of audit events for actor_id and session_id, include related_ids. (script: tools/export_audit_range.sh)
  2) Pull ephemeral session recording (if any) and attach to evidence bucket; generate evidence_refs value.
  3) Run heuristics: did actor have valid JIT session? was MFA used? was source IP allowlisted?
  4) Create JIRA-SEC ticket with pre-filled template and attach evidence_refs + filtered SIEM query link.
  5) Notify on #sec-ops and create Slack thread with triage checklist.
  6) Schedule access review if role was high-priv and action was allowed.
Automation implementation notes: use the canonical field names in step 1 to query SIEM (avoid service-specific fields).

6) Quick examples: SIEM queries and alerts
- Alert: privileged denial spike (Elastic PPL-like)
  query: event.action.keyword: ("manage:nodes" OR "kms:use") AND decision:"deny" AND env_tag:*
- Alert: new admin-binding outside normal cadence
  query: action:"bind:role" AND resource:"role:admin" AND NOT actor_id:(service-automation OR infra-ci)
- Forensics query: events for session_id S123 -> list all events where session_id:S123 sorted by timestamp

7) Data retention & evidence lifecycle (summary)
- Audit raw events: 2 years (cold storage after 90d)
- SIEM enriched indices: 13 months (hot/nearline)
- Evidence artifacts (session recordings, exports): 365 days by default; retention extended to 3 years for regulated customers on request.
- Deletion: automatic purge job with owner notification; keep manifest log for compliance.

8) Operational considerations / open items (TODOs)
- TODO: finalize CSV-vs-array contract for evidence_refs with logging team (Luca).
- TODO: add sample terraform policies for each snippet above (Dev Patel owns).
- Question: private environments — do we require HSM-provided key IDs in tenant manifest or only require key use via KMS? propose: require key-id annotation for any policy that includes kms:use.
- Action: schedule walkthrough with SRE and product-hosted-api to validate hosted operator deny-actions list. (owner: Aisha)

9) Quick glossary / codes
- DENY_ROLE: refused due to RBAC role mismatch
- DENY_NETWORK: refused because source IP not allowed by network-constraints
- JIT: Just-In-Time privileged session (ephemeral elevated token)

Appendix: sample evidence automation play command (ops)
- ./tools/collect-evidence --actor $ACTOR_ID --session $SESSION_ID --hours 24 --out /tmp/evidence_bundle.tgz
- After run: upload to s3://redwood-evidence/$TICKET_ID/ and record the S3 URI in evidence_refs

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally concise and operational — not a policy manifesto. Please comment inline on the choice of canonical field names, and on the practical deny-actions for hosted. We'll convert this into a longer 'security runbook' page in Confluence once we stabilize naming.

Change log (high level):
- 2024-09-03: initial draft by Priya
- 2025-02-07: added SIEM mapping and query examples (Luca)
- 2026-03-10: updated retention policy and private env HSM note (Aisha)

End.
